channel.title: Ballard & Fremont Dispatch
channel.description: Ballard & Fremont news, once a week, from the Ballard & Fremont Dispatch.

item.title: The first of this winter's highest tides peaks this morning and again Friday, under a coastal flood watch through 5 PM today
item.description: NOAA's Seattle tide gauge predicts 12.7 feet at 6:48 AM today and at 7:39 AM Friday, and more than 12 feet every morning through Monday.

item.title: Buses run a Sunday schedule today, the RapidRide D and E Lines included, and a regular weekday schedule Friday
item.description: Link's 1 and 2 Lines run a Sunday schedule today and a Saturday schedule Friday.

item.title: Every Seattle Public Library branch is closed today, and Green Lake and Wallingford stay closed Friday, their usual day off
item.description: Ballard and Greenwood open Friday 10 AM to 6 PM. The Fremont Branch on N 35th St is closed while a new heating, cooling and ventilation system goes in, and reopens in early 2027; its book return box is on the N 35th St side.

item.title: About the railroad bridge just west of the Ballard Locks: what the work is, how trains keep running, and when it will be done
item.description: Two readers asked about the railroad bridge just west of the Ballard Locks: what the work is, how trains keep running, and when it will be done.

item.title: Route 40's street work is finished through Ballard and Fremont
item.description: SDOT says major construction is done, with a ribbon cutting on October 29; crews may return for smaller tasks in the coming weeks.

item.title: A rezone at 6400 8th Ave NW would allow a six-story building with about 300 apartments
item.description: The application, filed October 26, asks for a contract rezone of the site from a 40-foot commercial zone and lowrise zoning to a 65-foot limit, for apartments, retail and 274 parking spaces below ground; the existing building would be demolished.

item.title: Ballard light rail's draft environmental study comes out December 11
item.description: Sound Transit opens a public comment period that day, running through February 9, with a hearing at the Nordic Museum on January 12.

item.title: the drain on your corner
item.description: Fallen leaves are the first thing to clog a storm drain, and a clogged drain floods the street around it in a hard rain.
